plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: A bulbous perennial that sends up goblet-shaped, crocus-like flowers directly from the ground in early autumn, long after its leaves have died back in summer. The leaves reappear the following spring. All parts are highly toxic.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to mid-autumn (September to October)
plants.location: Native to Europe and cultivated in temperate gardens worldwide, especially damp meadows and woodland edges in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.funFact: Colchicum is the source of colchicine, a compound used in medicine to treat gout, and it is also used by plant breeders to induce chromosome doubling. It is not related to true crocus or saffron.

plants.name: Aster novae-angliae
plants.description: A tall, robust perennial wildflower with hairy stems and masses of daisy-like flowers with yellow centers. It thrives in meadows, prairies, and roadsides, and is a vital late-season nectar source for pollinators.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to autumn (August to October)
plants.location: Eastern and central North America, from Canada to the southern United States; widely grown in cottage and pollinator gardens
plants.funFact: Monarch butterflies rely on New England asters as a key nectar source to fuel their long southward migration to Mexico each autumn.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A fast-growing deciduous to semi-evergreen tree with fern-like foliage that bursts into clouds of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers just before or as new leaves emerge. It creates striking purple carpets when blossoms drop.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring in the Southern Hemisphere (September to November)
plants.location: Native to South America; widely planted in Australia, South Africa (Pretoria), Argentina, and New Zealand's northern regions
plants.funFact: Pretoria in South Africa is nicknamed the Jacaranda City because tens of thousands of these trees line its streets, turning the city purple every October.

plants.name: Cosmos bipinnatus
plants.description: An airy annual with feathery foliage and daisy-like flowers on tall slender stems. It blooms profusely until the first frost and is easy to grow from seed in full sun and poor soil.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer to first frost (June to October)
plants.location: Native to Mexico and Central America; naturalized and cultivated across North America, Europe, and Asia
plants.funFact: Cosmos comes from the Greek word kosmos, meaning order or harmony, a name given by Spanish priests who grew them in mission gardens in Mexico.

plants.name: Osmanthus fragrans
plants.description: An evergreen shrub or small tree bearing clusters of tiny, intensely fragrant flowers with a scent of apricot and peach. It is a beloved ornamental in Chinese gardens and blooms in autumn.
plants.location: Native to Asia, including China, Japan, and the Himalayas; grown in warm temperate gardens including the southeastern United States
plants.funFact: In China, osmanthus blossoms are used to flavor teas, cakes, wine, and jams, and the Mid-Autumn Festival is traditionally celebrated with osmanthus cake and osmanthus wine.
